label: Smooth Maps and Manifolds with Corners
notes: This appendix, on printed pages 574 to 582, assembles the analytic toolkit used throughout the book: smoothness on spaces with corners, extension lemmas that promote local data to global, and an explicit bump construction. Treat it as the engine room behind every gluing and isotopy argument met earlier in the symplectic story.

label: Local Models with Corners
notes: Manifolds with corners are modeled on quadrant-type sets, the product of half-lines with a Euclidean factor. We test smoothness by demanding that, in every chart, a map extend smoothly across the boundary into the open ambient space, so derivatives of all orders exist one-sidedly and agree across faces.

label: Why Corners Appear
notes: Corners are not pathology; they are forced. A product of two manifolds with boundary already has a corner along the product of the boundaries, and compactified moduli spaces of holomorphic curves carry strata where several breaking parameters vanish at once. The appendix exists to handle these spaces honestly rather than excise them.

label: Strata of a Corner Chart
notes: The quadrant decomposes into strata by counting vanishing coordinates: the open interior, two boundary edges where one coordinate is zero, and the single corner point where both vanish. Smoothness on the whole quadrant is strictly stronger than smoothness restricted to each stratum, since mixed cross-derivatives must match at the corner.

label: Smoothness via Charts
notes: A map between manifolds with corners is smooth when every local representative, read through charts, is the restriction of a genuinely smooth map on an open neighborhood. Equivalently, all partial derivatives extend continuously to the boundary faces. This definition is chart-independent because the transition maps are themselves smooth in exactly this sense.

label: The Extension Lemma
notes: The central technical result: a map smooth on an open set containing a closed subset, or defined along a submanifold, extends to a smooth map on a neighborhood of that set. The proof patches local Taylor data with a partition of unity, so no single chart ever needs to see the whole subset at once.

label: Extending Sections
notes: The extension principle applies to sections of vector bundles, not only to functions. A section defined over a closed subset or submanifold extends to a smooth global section after multiplying by a cutoff supported near the set. This is exactly how vector fields and almost complex structures are propagated outward in the main text.

label: The Standard Smooth Function
notes: Everything rests on one function: exponential of minus one over x for positive x and zero otherwise. It is smooth at the origin because every derivative is a rational expression times the exponential, which decays faster than any polynomial blows up, forcing all one-sided derivatives to vanish at zero.

label: Bump and Cutoff Functions
notes: From the standard function we build a smooth cutoff: flat at one near the origin, descending, then flat at zero outside a chosen radius. Multiplying one-variable bumps gives plateaus on balls and on quadrant collars near corners, providing the localizers that every patching argument in this book silently uses.

label: Partitions of Unity
notes: Subordinate to any open cover of a manifold with corners there is a smooth partition of unity: nonnegative bumps, each supported in one cover element, summing to one. Local finiteness makes the sum well defined, and the cutoff construction supplies the individual functions even across boundary faces and corners.

label: Gluing Local to Global
notes: Partitions of unity convert agreement on overlaps into a single global object. Locally defined smooth maps, metrics, or forms are averaged with the partition weights to produce a global smooth object that restricts correctly. This averaging is the recurring move behind existence theorems for the structures studied in the book.

label: Recap and Use
notes: We collected the smooth-category infrastructure: corner models, the stratified quadrant, chart-based smoothness, the extension lemmas for maps and sections, the exponential bump, and partitions of unity. Together they let local symplectic constructions be glued into global ones with full control over boundary and corner behavior throughout the book.
